And the child, if he comes here before me, console him.
Being soothed by the gentle, guileless consolations of pure anointing.
Thus I corrected for φοινίσσαμυγμοῖς [bloody gashes], which arose from the gloss φοίνισσομένη [being reddened] written beside αἱματοῦσσα [bloody].

They counted their virgin life as nothing.
Why do you remain a virgin so long?
For I fear a virginity that hates men.
And it is lawful to desire a virgin's blood.

in the verses of the interpolator Παρθενοπαῖος Ἀρκάς · ὁ δὲ τοιόσδ᾽ ἀνήρ – [Parthenopaeus the Arcadian; and such a man –] where the second syllable is lengthened, as if it should be pronounced Παρθεννοπαῖος [Parthennopaeus]: about which I have spoken on Sophocles fr. 285 in the third Oxford edition and in the Prolegomena to the Tragic Poets p. 33. Aeschylus undoubtedly used the same meter in the verse supplied by me after v. 525, Παρθενοπαῖον Ἀρκάδ᾽, Ἀταλάντης γόνον [Parthenopaeus the Arcadian, offspring of Atalanta].
Parthenopaeus the Arcadian; and such a man –

And the virgins who dwell in the land of Colchis.
Do you hear the voice of the cow-horned maiden?
See the suppliant band of maidens.
Cruel, not a mind named after maidens.
Or the virgin daughter of Zeus, Justice.
With the watery streams of the maiden's spring.
Upon the delicate luxuries of maidens.
The Ister gives birth to such maidens.
To pure maidens who have not tasted the marriage bed.
And a lock of hair like that of delicate maidens.
Defiling his father's hands with streams of a slaughtered virgin.
